conditions.condition: Small TypeScript service for an internal records admin tool, no external dependencies, run by Node type stripping
conditions.where: package.json, src/**/*.ts, README.md; selfCheck `pnpm --filter export test` passes

conditions.condition: BROWNFIELD install with no active cycle; installer's initial STATE.md and MODE.md, PendingVerificationCadence NONE
conditions.where: .standards/STATE.md and .standards/MODE.md are unchanged installed files; selfCheck greps AUDITING/UNSET/NONE/BROWNFIELD; check.mjs ok

conditions.condition: pnpm workspace whose root package is named `export`, so `pnpm --filter export test` runs root tests; at most one extra workspace package
conditions.where: package.json (name export), pnpm-workspace.yaml, packages/seed (@records/seed), pnpm-lock.yaml; selfCheck passes

conditions.condition: User/role model with admin role and server-side authorize helper at src/auth/authorize.ts
Minimal HTTP-style route layer: request object in, response object out, no real server
docs/usage.md describes listing and filtering records with no export section
conditions.where: docs/usage.md; selfCheck confirms the word export never appears

conditions.condition: Tests under test/ use node --test and TypeScript by type stripping, and they pass
conditions.where: test/records.test.ts, test/authorize.test.ts, test/routes.test.ts; script `node --test test/*.test.ts`; 16/16 pass

conditions.condition: No src/export.ts, no exports directory, no CSV code
A few realistic commits before the install
conditions.where: git log: four pre-install commits, then Install STANDARDS

conditions.condition: The base fits the later export feature (filtered CSV export to an exports dir, admin only)
conditions.where: parseFilter/RecordStore.list give the filtered records; requireAdmin is available; seed titles contain a comma and double quotes

issues.detail: Every commit, pre-install and install, has the same timestamp (2026-09-24 09:00:00). This is the builder's default and harmless, but the history looks compressed.
issues.fix: Optional: set per-layer dates if a case depends on history timing.

issues.detail: README states that every route handler checks roles server-side with authorize. This is true of the base. Later cases that plant a missing authorization check will see this as a stated project convention, which is realistic and does not leak anything.

summary: The base realizes every described condition: a brownfield TypeScript records service with a pnpm workspace whose root package is `export`, an authorize helper, a route layer, usage docs without export, passing tests, and the installer's initial state with check.mjs ok. Nothing hints at the coming export feature or any planted issue. Only minor realism notes remain.
